preconditions.description: The number of acorns n is between 1 and 500,000 inclusive.
The input sequence a has exactly 2n - 1 integers.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= x <= n for x in a)
preconditions.description: Each element in the input sequence is an integer between 0 and n inclusive, where 0 represents an illegible number.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'no' if not exists_valid_tour else output_lines[0] == 'yes'
postconditions.description: The first line of output is 'no' if no valid Euler tour exists matching the constraints, otherwise it is 'yes'. Here, exists_valid_tour is true if there exists a sequence b of length 2n-1 satisfying the Euler tour properties and matching non-zero entries in a.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'yes' implies (len(output_lines) == 2 and len(b) == 2 * n - 1 and all(b[i] == a[i] or a[i] == 0 for i in range(2 * n - 1)) and all(1 <= x <= n for x in b) and b[0] == b[-1] and len(set(b)) == n and all(is_adjacent_in_tree(b[i], b[i+1]) for i in range(2 * n - 2)))
postconditions.description: If the output is 'yes', the second line contains a sequence b of length 2n-1. This sequence b must match the input a at all non-zero positions, contain only integers from 1 to n, start and end with the same value, contain every integer from 1 to n at least once, and consist of consecutive elements that are adjacent in some tree structure.
If the output is 'no', no sequence b exists that satisfies the Euler tour definition and matches the non-zero constraints of the input.
